newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan made no commitment to U.S. on growth - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan made no commitment to U.S. on growth - MOF.

text.p: Japan did not make a commitment to the United States concerning its policy of seeking growth led by domestic demand, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Wednesday.
Asked whether Japan had made a commitment to the United States, Mitsuzuka said: "The bottom line is that there was no commitment."

Deputy U.S. Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said on Tuesday after talks with Mitsuzuka that he welcomed a commitment by Japan to take measures as needed to ensure a recovery led by strong domestic demand and to avoid a significant rise in its trade surplus.
Mitsuzuka said Summers had voiced concern about Japan's current account and trade surpluses, bringing up the example of a recent rise in car exports.
But Mitsuzuka said the government's goal of 1.9 percent economic growth in 1997/98, starting on April 1, would be achieved by a rise domestic demand and would not rely on external demand.
He said: "The Japanese economy has firmness and underlying strength. It will be able to more than cover (the negative effects of fiscal tightening measures to be carried out from April)."

The Lower House of Japan's parliament earlier on Wednesday approved a state budget totalling 77.39 trillion yen for the fiscal year starting on April 1. It will now go to the Upper House for approval before becoming law.

Summers, in Tokyo for a meeting of Asia-Pacific economies, said on Tuesday that his discussions with Mitsuzuka, Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita and other senior Japanese officials covered the current outlook for the Japanese economy.

He said he expressed the desire of the United States that Japan pursue a supportive macroeconomic policy stance necessary to promote a strong recovery led by domestic demand and to prevent a resurgence in Japan's external surplus.

"Minister of Finance Mitsuzuka made it clear that the Japanese government shared these objectives and he committed to take measures as necessary to ensure a strong demand-led recovery and avoid a significant increase in external imbalances," he said.
